([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]) | draftyear = 2023 | draftpick = 4 | draftround = 1 | draftteam = [[Houston Rockets]] | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = Team OTE | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = City Reapers | years3 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team3 = [[Houston Rockets]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = →[[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] ({{nbay|2024|end}}) * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2023|end}}) * [[Overtime Elite|OTE]] champion (2023) * All-OTE First Team (2023) }} '''Ameiz XLNC''' "'''Amen'''" '''Thompson''' ({{IPAc-en|ə|ˈ|m|ɛ|n|_|ˈ|ɛ|k|s|ə|l|ə|n|s|_|ˈ|t|ɒ|m|s|ə|n}} {{respelling|ə|MEN|_|EK|sə|lənss|_|TOM|sən}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born January 30, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played basketball for [[Pine Crest School]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]], where he was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and won a state title. Thompson bypassed his senior year of high school to sign with [[Overtime Elite|OTE]], where he played for two seasons and helped his team win the league title while earning All-OTE First Team honors in 2023. He was selected 4th overall in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the Houston Rockets. In 2024, he made the NBA [[NBA All-Rookie Team|All-Rookie Second Team]], and in 2025 he was named to the NBA [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive first team]]. He is the twin brother of basketball player [[Ausar Thompson]]. ==Early life== Thompson was born to Maya Wilson and Troy Thompson and raised in [[San Leandro, California]].{{cite web |last=Gutierrez |first=Israel |title=The Thompson twins and Overtime Elite's unproven path to the NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34487913 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=August 31, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Polacheck |first=Jacob |title=An Audacious Dream Meets Itself in Reality: A Look Inside Overtime Elite's Inaugural Season |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2022/04/18/an-audacious-dream-meets-itself-in-reality-a-look-inside-overtime-elites-inaugural-season/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=April 18, 2022}} He is of Jamaican descent through his father.{{Cite web|url=https://thecaribbeancamera.com/twin-brothers-of-jamaican-heritage-make-history-in-nba-draft/|title=Twin brothers of Jamaican heritage make history in NBA draft|author=The Caribbean Camera Inc|date=July 15, 2023|website=The Caribbean Camera}} His identical twin brother, [[Ausar Thompson|Ausar]], was born one minute after him; they share the middle name "XLNC" (pronounced "''excellence''").{{cite web |last=Graham |first=Pat |title=Twins Amen and Ausar Thompson set to be taken in top-10 of NBA draft |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/twins-amen-ausar-thompson-set-top-10-nba-100249856 |website=ABC News |access-date=May 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623063213/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/twins-amen-ausar-thompson-set-top-10-nba-100249856 |archive-date=June 23, 2023 |date=June 20, 2023}} Thompson's older brother, Troy Jr., played [[college basketball]] for [[Prairie View A&M Panthers basketball|Prairie View A&M]]. His uncle, [[Mark Thompson (hurdler)|Mark Thompson]], represented [[Jamaica]] in [[Athletics at the 1992 Summer Olympics – Men's 400 metres hurdles|400 meter hurdles]] at the [[1992 Summer Olympics]]. He and Ausar began training for basketball under the guidance of their father by age seven and drew inspiration from [[LeBron James]]. The twins were [[homeschooled]] in sixth and seventh grades to focus on basketball. ==High school career== Entering eighth grade, Thompson and his family moved to [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] so that he and Ausar could play high school basketball one year early at [[Pine Crest School]].{{cite web |last=Schoenfield |first=Bruce |title=The Teenagers Getting Six Figures to Leave Their High Schools for Basketball |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/30/magazine/overtime-elite-basketball-nba.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 26, 2023 |date=November 30, 2021}} The twins immediately started for the team.{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=David |title='I did not think we were going to win': Pine Crest wins state title with miracle comeback |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/prep-broward/article249715043.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 6, 2021}} As a sophomore at Pine Crest, Thompson averaged 16.9 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game, earning All-[[Broward County, Florida|County]] honorable mention. Entering his junior season, he was named to the Broward County Fab Five by the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]''.{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |title=Broward County boys basketball Fab Five for 2020 (and the next five) |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-fab-five-broward-2020-20201215-xchw56365nft5kj73jym3z7uw4-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=December 15, 2020}} He averaged 20.5 points, 8.4 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game as a junior, leading his team to the Class 4A state championship in a 90–83 double [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over [[Santa Fe High School (Florida)|Santa Fe High School]].{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |title=Broward 5A-1A boys basketball co-players of the year: Ausar Thompson and Amen Thompson, Pine Crest juniors |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-county/fl-sp-ss-prem-ac-br-bhoop-small-poy-20210328-qjyzjbndyndqpksczpjufut46q-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=March 27, 2021}} In the title game, Thompson scored 43 points and helped Pine Crest overcome an eight-point deficit with 45 seconds left in overtime. He shared Broward County Class 5A-1A co-player of the year honors from the ''Sun-Sentinel'' with Ausar. ===Recruiting=== Thompson was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson - Basketball Recruiting |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/243378 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 27, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Amen Thompson, 2022 Point Guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/amen-thompson-260426?view=pv |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 27, 2023}} He gained interest from college programs in 2019, receiving a scholarship offer from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |last=Young |first=Justin |title=South Florida's Thompson Twins are catching on with recruiters |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/player/201910/south-floridas-thompson-twins-are-catching-recruiters |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 27, 2023 |date=October 2, 2019}} After his junior year, Thompson held offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], among other programs, before deciding to not play [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last=Branham |first=Travis |date=May 25, 2021 |title=Elite twins Amen and Ausar Thompson skip college to join the Overtime Elite program scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 overall = | rivals overall = | espn overall = | accessdate = January 28, 2023 | bball = yes }} ==Professional career== === Team OTE (2021–2022) === On May 25, 2021, Thompson signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in [[Atlanta]] with players between ages 16 and 20. He joined the league with his brother Ausar, bypassing his final year of high school and college, because he felt that it would prepare him best for the NBA.{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle |title=Overtime Elite lands another set of twins as Amen and Ausar Thompson choose professional program over college |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/overtime-elite-lands-another-set-of-twins-as-amen-and-ausar-thompson-choose-professional-program-over-college/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=May 25, 2021}}{{cite magazine |last=Woo |first=Jeremy |title=Can Overtime Elite Disrupt Basketball With ... Twins? |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/03/07/overtime-elite-thompson-twins-daily-cover |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 7, 2022}} In the 2021–22 season, Thompson played for Team OTE, one of three teams in the league, and averaged 14 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.1 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Araiza |first=Robert |title=Amen & Ausar Thompson: Should the San Antonio Spurs roll the dice? |url=https://airalamo.com/posts/amen-ausar-thompson-should-san-antonio-spurs-roll-dice/2 |publisher=Air Alamo |agency=[[FanSided]]|access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023}}{{cite web |last=Sprung |first=Shlomo |title=Overtime Elite Roster 2022-23 |url=https://boardroom.tv/overtime-elite-roster-2022-23/ |publisher=Boardroom |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=August 26, 2022}} He competed against other OTE teams, as well as [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] and [[Postgraduate year|postgraduate]] opponents.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Overtime Elite announces 2021-22 schedule, roster for inaugural season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32381206 |access-date=January 28, 2023 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} He helped his team achieve a runner-up finish, scoring 13 points in a 52–45 loss to Team Elite in the decisive third game of the finals.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Team Elite Wins First Overtime Elite Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b82a7362-6679-4e97-be6a-bf55e3294708 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=March 14, 2022 |archive-date=July 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713045305/https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b82a7362-6679-4e97-be6a-bf55e3294708 |url-status=dead }} Thompson played for OTE affiliate Team Overtime in [[The Basketball Tournament 2022|The Basketball Tournament]] in July 2022. His team lost to Omaha Blue Crew, 74–70, in the first round of the tournament.{{cite web |last=DeMarinis |first=Matt |title=Omaha Blue Crew outlasts Team Overtime in a battle of old versus new |url=https://whiteandbluereview.com/omaha-blue-crew-outlasts-team-overtime-in-a-battle-of-old-versus-new/ |publisher=White and Blue Review |access-date=January 28, 2021 |date=July 17, 2022}} === City Reapers (2022–2023) === In the 2022–23 OTE season, Thompson played for the City Reapers alongside team [[captain (sports)|captain]] Ausar, who selected him with the first pick in the league's draft.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=OTE Announces Roster Reveal and Expansion for Season 2 |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d8ad12ca-acbd-44d1-b6d9-9f5f1c5def45 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=September 21, 2022 |archive-date=July 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713045525/https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d8ad12ca-acbd-44d1-b6d9-9f5f1c5def45 |url-status=dead }} On January 9, 2023, he was named OTE Player of the Week, three days after recording 22 points, 10 rebounds, seven assists and five steals in a 101–90 win over the Cold Hearts.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Amen Thompson named OTE Player of the Week |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/83f18057-c9a9-4f28-b926-2592e600c537 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=January 28, 2023 |date=January 9, 2023}} In the regular season, Thompson averaged 16.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 2.3 steals per game and was named to the All-OTE First Team.{{Cite web |date=February 20, 2023 |title=OTE Announces Regular Season Awards |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/b66abb33-0079-4dc0-9858-7f6933f9a54a |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=OTE |archive-date=May 15, 2023 2023 |url=https://overtimeelite.com/players/e763b02b-3045-4a91-a078-7140899327d0/career |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023}} In game 2 of the OTE Finals, he made a game-winning layup at the buzzer in an 80–78 win over the YNG Dreamerz.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=Amen Sinks Buzzer Beater for Reapers Game 2 Win |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/d021e545-7230-4b6d-af97-e01e51ee40f3 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023 |date=March 4, 2023 |archive-date=March 31, 2023 championship in a 3–0 [[Whitewash (sport)|sweep]].{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Joseph |title=City Reapers Win OTE Championship |url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/81ad0922-4800-435b-9706-a5a6180ceb56 |publisher=[[Overtime Elite]] |access-date=June 19, 2023 |date=March 4, 2023 |archive-date=March 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331070347/https://www.overtimeelite.com/articles/81ad0922-4800-435b-9706-a5a6180ceb56 |url-status=dead }} On April 21, 2023, he declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]], where analysts viewed him as a potential top-10 pick.{{cite web |last=Cobb |first=David |title=2023 NBA Draft: Amen, Ausar Thompson declare as likely lottery picks after playing for Overtime Elite |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2023-nba-draft-amen-ausar-thompson-declare-as-likely-lottery-picks-after-playing-for-overtime-elite/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=June 18, 2023 |date=April 21, 2023}} ===Houston Rockets (2023–present)=== The [[Houston Rockets]] selected Thompson with the fourth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]], one pick ahead of his twin brother [[Ausar Thompson|Ausar]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/amen-thompson-rockets-no-4-pick-2023-nba-draft|title=Amen Thompson: Meet the Rockets' No. 4 pick in 2023 NBA Draft|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 22, 2023}} They were the first brothers in NBA draft history to be selected in the top 5 in the same year.{{Cite web |last=Woodyard |first=Eric |date=June 23, 2023 |title=Amen, Ausar Thompson first brothers taken in top 5 of same NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story?id=37902522 |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} He made his NBA debut on October 25, 2023, scoring eight points along with five rebounds and two assists in a 116–86 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets 86-116 Magic (Oct 25, 2023) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401584694 |access-date=2023-10-26 |website=ESPN |language=en}} He went on to miss a several games around start of the season after suffering a Grade 2 ankle sprain on his left ankle. He was sent to the G-League on December 5 for development before being recalled from the Rockets four days later.{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=December 5, 2023 |title=Rockets rookie Amen Thompson returns from injury with NBA G League assignment |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/05/rockets-rookie-amen-thompson-returns-from-injury-with-nba-g-league-assignment/ |website=rocketswire.usatoday.com}} He made his return on the bench after a 15-game absence and recorded two points, five rebounds, and one assist in 10 minutes in the 93–82 win over the San Antonio Spurs. His minutes and numbers increased while playing full-time in the starting lineup for the final 15 games of the season after teammate [[Alperen Şengün]] missed the closing weeks of the season due to a knee injury.{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=March 12, 2024 |title=With Alperen Sengun injured, Rockets promote Amen Thompson to starting lineup |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2024/03/12/with-alperen-sengun-injured-rockets-promote-amen-thompson-to-starting-lineup/ |access-date=March 12, 2024 |website=rocketswire.usatoday.com}} In the final game of his rookie season, Thompson recorded his first triple-double in a win against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with totals of 18 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists.{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |date=April 14, 2024 |title=Takeaways: Amen Thompson posts first triple-double, Rockets beat Clippers to clinch .500 season |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/lists/takeaways-amen-thompson-posts-first-triple-double-rockets-beat-clippers-to-clinch-500-season/ |access-date=April 14, 2024 |website=rocketswire.usatoday.com}} He was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] and became the fifth Rockets player to receive NBA All-Rookie recognition within the last four seasons.{{cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/amen-thompson-all-rookie-second-team-selection-19468436.php|title=Houston Rockets' Amen Thompson earns NBA All-Rookie second team honors|website=Houston Chronicle|last=Feigen|first=Jonathan|date=May 20, 2024|access-date=January 8, 2025}} On December 30, 2024, Thompson was ejected from a game against the [[Miami Heat]] following a confrontation with Heat guard [[Tyler Herro]] with only 35 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter of a tight contest. While the two were battling for position during an inbounds play, Thompson grabbed Herro by the jersey and threw him to the ground. The incident occurred just moments after Thompson's teammate, [[Fred VanVleet]], was ejected for bumping a referee. The altercation pulled in teammates and coaching staff from both teams, and six individuals were ultimately ejected, being Thompson, Herro, Rockets guard [[Jalen Green]], Rockets head coach [[Ime Udoka]], Rockets assistant coach [[Ben Sullivan (basketball)|Ben Sullivan]], and Heat guard [[Terry Rozier]]. The Rockets finished ended with a defeat at home with a final score of 102–100. Following the loss to the Heat, Thompson received a two-game suspension.{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2024 |title=Amen Thompson-Tyler Herro fight leads to ejections of multiple players and coaches in Heat’s victory in Houston |url=https://www.nba.com/news/amen-thompson-tyler-herro-fight-leads-to-ejections-of-multiple-players-and-coaches-in-heats-victory-in-houston |access-date=December 30, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} Thompson took a major role in January–February when he started in the line-up for the injured [[Jabari Smith Jr.]]. On January 5, 2025, he put up 23 points alongside a then career-high 16 rebounds in a 119–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/rockets-news-amen-thompson-breaks-silence-monster-game-vs-lakers-after-suspension|title=Rockets' Amen Thompson breaks silence on monster game vs. Lakers after suspension|website=ClutchPoints|last=Bologna|first=Ryan|date=January 5, 2025|access-date=January 8, 2025}} On January 27, he put up a then career-high 33 points and the game-winning shot in a 114–112 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-jaylen-brown-jayson-tatum-react-dillon-brooks-career-high-10-threes|title=Celtics' Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum react to Dillon Brook's career-high 10 threes|website=ClutchPoints|last=Donabedian|first=Daniel|date=January 27, 2025|access-date=January 27, 2025}} At the conclusion of the season, he was named to his first [[NBA All-Defensive Team]], becoming the fifth Rockets player to receive the honor.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-amen-thompson-named-kia-nba-all-defensive-first-team|title=Rockets Amen Thompson Named Kia NBA All-Defensive First Team|website=nba.com|date=May 22, 2025|access-date=January 28, 2026}} On January 26, 2026, Thompson put up a career-high 14 assists alongside eight points, eight rebounds, and one steal in a 108–99 win over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/houston-rockets/rockets-news-amen-thompson-breaks-personal-record-grizzlies-game|title=Rockets’ Amen Thompson breaks personal record in Grizzlies game|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=January 26, 2026|access-date=January 28, 2026}} On April 10, he scored a career-high 41 points on 17-of-22 shooting in a 132–136 loss against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On September 3, 2026, Thompson signed a five-year, $208 million extension with the Rockets.{{Cite web|title=Amen Thompson signs five-year extension with Rockets|url=https://www.nba.com/news/amen-thompson-5-year-extension-rockets|website=NBA.com|date=September 3, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA===
